derivedFrom.note: Every value carries an `evidence` field. Values without one are inferred from the rules, not measured directly.

evidence.note: Icons not at 2.0 are solid masses with no stroke to measure, not counter-examples.

terminals.buttCapWhen: the stroke terminates against, or aligns with, another form
terminals.divergesFromMaterial: Material 1 specifies squared terminals; Open Icons is round-dominant. Intentional.

squareContainerCorner.note: outer - inner = 1.94 ~= stroke; smoothing survives the offset

opticalSize.model: discrete masters, not a variable axis

evidence.interpretation: p25-p75 brackets the two keyline ratios exactly: 1.25 (circle 16->20) and 1.286 (square 14->18). Glyph tracks its keyline; nothing tracks the canvas.

opticalSize.rule: Never scale a master. Re-place the skeleton on the new size's keyline and re-stroke at 2.
opticalSize.materialRange: 20-48dp; Open Icons' 16px master sits below Material's floor

strokeModel.kRationale: k=1.0 is pure linear scaling — the stroke/size ratio stays flat, which means zero optical compensation. k=0 is what the current 16/24 masters do (both 2.0), correct at the small end but it collapses at display sizes. k=0.8 lightens the icon ~20% relatively across a 3x size jump, which is conservative next to what text does from body to display optical sizes. Lower k to 0.75 for more differentiation, raise to 0.85 for less. This is the one number to argue about.

quantize.why: 0.25 steps only resolve crisply at 4x DPR. At 16-24px the stroke is only 1-2px total, so sub-pixel blur is visible; above 32px a half-pixel soft edge on a multi-pixel stroke is not.

notes: 300 at 16px computes to 0.72 and is unusable. 16px ships 400 and 600 only.
20px is the one size the pixel grid forces a compromise: 1.30 raw sits between 1.0 and 1.5. Shipping 1.5 makes 20px the relatively boldest size in the set, which is defensible for a dense-UI size.
The existing 24px library at stroke 2.0 IS the 600 master under this model — no redrawing needed.
The existing 16px library at stroke 2.0 is heavier than 600@16 (1.5). It is effectively a 700. Either re-stroke it to 1.5, or label 16px as a deliberately one-step-bold dense master.

lineToFill.invariant: A fill variant never extends beyond its line variant's outer edge.

container.when: the outer form is a frame (circle, square) holding a glyph
container.rule: Container goes solid at the SAME outer radius. Reuse the glyph path verbatim as an even-odd knockout.

figure.when: a stroked ring becomes a solid mass with nothing inside it
figure.anchor: Pin the contact datum (e.g. the head's bottom tangent); move the centre to keep it fixed.

reshapingLadder.why: Under the weight model, 400 resolves to 1.5 at 24px and 1.0 at 16px — both exactly 6.25% of canvas. The 0.5px quantization flattens the optical exponent to 1.0 across the two key sizes, so no stroke-based optical compensation is available at 16px. It comes from aperture instead: measured modal clearance is 2.0 at BOTH sizes, so the glyph shrinks x0.8 while gaps hold absolute, leaving the small icon relatively looser.

clearanceRule.validation: reproduces the measured library exactly: 2px stroke -> 2.0 clearance

steps.do: Scale the glyph to the target keyline (x0.8 for 24 -> 16).
Re-stroke at the target size's value. Never scale the stroke.
Hold clearance >= 1 x stroke, absolute. This IS the optical compensation.
Reduce counts until (3) is satisfied — within an element, not by deleting it.
Marks scale with the keyline, floor Ø2.5 at 16px. Hold absolute only when scaling drops clearance below 1 x stroke.
Corners stay squircle at every size; ease `tension` toward circular as size drops.

decisions.question: marks: scale or hold
decisions.rationale: Holding breaks on cart — its wheels already sit on the bottom edge at Ø2.5; Ø3 pushes them out of the box.

decisions.question: overflow: drop or reduce
decisions.rationale: Keeps the icon's full vocabulary at every size.

decisions.question: corners across sizes
decisions.rationale: Corner family is a system constant; size adjusts the lever, not the family.

reshapingLadder.note: All three decisions make the existing 16px masters non-conforming. Expected — 24px is the reference and 16px is being redrawn to match.

counters.rule: Counters that flip from positive ink to knockout GROW. They never shrink.
counters.rationale: aperture closure at 16-24px beats optical bleed compensation
counters.divergesFromMaterial: Material's grade -25 THINS light-on-dark to cancel visual bleed. Open Icons runs the opposite sign, locally, on apertures only.

seamGap.meaning: two forms read as ONE body with a seam, not two separate objects

evidence.note: Both variants centre on 2.0; fill concentrates harder on it. Line tolerates 1.0-1.5 far more often.

figure.description: person / people family. The most rigorously specified group in the set.
construction: Draw the head SKELETON circle (r=4 @ (12,7) for 24px; r=3 @ (8,4) for 16px).
Line: stroke at 2 -> outer r=5. Head bottom lands on the datum.
Fill: solid disc at outer - 0.5, centre moved DOWN 0.5 so the bottom tangent stays pinned.
Shoulder top = head bottom + 1, in both variants.

group-circles-4.reason: abstract circle diagram, not a figure

crossout.description: the X. Two 45-degree skeleton strokes crossing at the live-area centre.
crossout.evidence: barWidth measured at exactly 2.000 in every crossout variant, both sizes: standalone, in-circle, in-square, and prohibited.

contained.rule: inside a container the glyph shrinks to ~70% and clears the container's inner edge by ~1

slashVariant.fillConstruction: keeps the ring; adds an inner disc split by a 2-unit diagonal gap, 2 units clear of the ring
slashVariant.note: The one fill variant that is NOT a solid disc. Everything in it is 2. Diverges from the container pattern - flag for consistency review.

steps: Container = circle keyline (r=10 at 24px, r=8 at 16px) or square keyline.
Line: container as a 2px ring. Glyph as positive ink, clearing the ring's inner edge by ~1.
Fill: container becomes a solid disc at the SAME outer radius; reuse the glyph path unchanged as an even-odd knockout.
Apply counter compensation ONLY if the glyph has small round counters or internal gaps.

lintRules.assert: fill silhouette never exceeds line silhouette at any angle
a counter flipping positive -> knockout must not decrease in radius
16px master is not a uniform scale of the 24px master (expected glyph scale ~1.25, not 1.5)
ink bbox matches a keyline on at least one axis
container icons reuse the line glyph path verbatim in the fill variant
figure icons use a head-to-shoulder gap of exactly 1.0
no two icon names share identical path geometry
every -line icon has a -fill partner and vice versa
every icon exists at both 16 and 24
